ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is it important to plan a composition? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you from writing
   B. It makes the story longer without ideas
   C. It hides your ideas
   D. It keeps the ideas in order

2. What is tax? (1 mark)
   A. Money that people pay to the government
   B. Money given as a prize
   C. A kind of market
   D. A bank loan

3. Which is the correct spelling? (1 mark)
   A. necesary
   B. neccessary
   C. necessary
   D. necessery

4. Which preposition completes: 'He borrowed money ____ his uncle.'? (1 mark)
   A. of
   B. at
   C. from
   D. by

5. What does 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Nine stitches are better than one
   B. Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   C. Time is money
   D. Sewing is always fun

6. Which sentence asks about time and needs a question mark at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Please sit down
   B. We won the match
   C. The match starts at ten
   D. When does the match start

7. Why should you return borrowed books on time? (1 mark)
   A. To make the book dirty
   B. So others can read them too
   C. Because books are heavy
   D. To forget the title

8. Which sentence uses 'nor' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   B. She has no soap, nor she does have water.
   C. She has no soap, nor water has she.
   D. She has no soap nor does have water she.

9. In netball, what must a player do with the ball after catching it? (1 mark)
   A. Kick it
   B. Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   C. Run with it
   D. Sit on it

10. Which preposition completes: 'She put the coins ____ the tin.'? (1 mark)
   A. opposite
   B. beside
   C. into
   D. between

11. What does 'profit' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. Money lost in a sale
   C. Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   D. A tax

12. Which is an example of a nonverbal cue? (1 mark)
   A. A word
   B. A thumbs-up
   C. A sentence
   D. A song

13. Which is the best thing to do if an online message makes you afraid? (1 mark)
   A. Send it to all your friends
   B. Reply to the stranger
   C. Keep it a secret
   D. Show it to a trusted adult at once

14. What is the comparative of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. more happy
   B. happyer
   C. happier
   D. happiest

15. Which is the adverb form of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. happiy
   B. happily
   C. happly
   D. happyly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write four sentences using in, on, under and between. (4 marks)

17. Explain when we use some and when we use any. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

18. Write three yes/no questions about keeping the compound clean. (3 marks)

19. Give two nonverbal cues that show a speaker is confident. (2 marks)

20. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — It keeps the ideas in order
   A plan shows what comes first, next and last.

2. A — Money that people pay to the government
   Tax pays for services such as roads and schools.

3. C — necessary
   One c and two s's.

4. C — from
   We borrow from someone.

5. B — Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   Early action saves later work.

6. D — When does the match start
   It is a direct question.

7. B — So others can read them too
   It shows responsibility and fairness.

8. A — She has no soap, nor does she have water.
   After 'nor', the helping verb comes before the subject.

9. B — Pass it within three seconds without running with it
   The passage says players cannot run with the ball.

10. C — into
   She moved the coins to the inside.

11. C — Money gained when you sell for more than you paid
   Profit is the gain from selling.

12. B — A thumbs-up
   Gestures are nonverbal.

13. D — Show it to a trusted adult at once
   A trusted adult can help you stay safe.

14. C — happier
   Change y to i and add er.

15. B — happily
   Change y to i and add -ly.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The coins are in the box. The book is on the table. The cat is under the chair. The shop is between the bank and the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: Some is used in positive sentences and polite offers: I have some books. Any is used in questions and negatives: Do you have any books?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule and 1 mark for each example.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Do you sweep the compound? Is the bin covered? Can we plant a tree?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct question.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Eye contact and standing straight; a smile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is reading quickly to get the main idea; scanning is looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
